Rashi on Shabbat 103b:10:1.hebrew: מ"ט דר' יוסי - היכי דריש ליה:
Rashi on Shabbat 103b:10:1.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yosei - How does he expound it?

Rashi on Shabbat 103b:10:2.hebrew: אחת מאחת - אחת ה"ל למכתב ולשתוק, וכתב מ"ם יתירה [ומהנה יתירא]:
Rashi on Shabbat 103b:10:2.english: One, from one - [Scripture] should have written "one" and stopped, yet it wrote a superfluous mem [and "from these" is superfluous].

Rashi on Shabbat 103b:10:3.hebrew: הנה מהנה - א"נ, הנה הוה ליה למכתב וכתב מהנה — מ"ם יתירה, ומאחת יתירה. הלכך, למדרשינהו לכולהו כתבינהו, ודרוש אחת הנה בלא מ"ם הכי: אחת שהיא הנה, הנה שהיא אחת. לתרי גווני איכא למידרש משמעותייהו: ועשה עבירה אחת והיא לו הנה — חייב חטאות הרבה; אי נמי, ועשה אחת — עשייתו חשובה לו כאחת, ואע"פ שהנה היו — משמע שהרבה עבירות עשה, והיינו הנה שהיא אחת. הלכך תרוייהו דריש ביה: פעמים שהיא כן, ופעמים שהיא כן, כדמפרש לקמיה:
Rashi on Shabbat 103b:10:3.english: These, of these - Alternatively, [the verse] should have written "these" and it wrote "of these" — an extra mem, and "of one" is [also] extra. Therefore, [Scripture] wrote all of them in order to expound them all; and expound "one" [and] "these" without a mem as follows: "one" that is "these," [and] "these" that is "one." Their meaning can be expounded in two ways: "and he did" one transgression and it is [reckoned] for him as "these" — he is liable for many sin-offerings; or else, "and he did one" — his act is reckoned for him as one, even though they were "these" — [which] implies that he committed many transgressions, and this is "these" that is "one." Therefore, he expounds both [ways] from it: sometimes it is like this, and sometimes it is like that, as [the Gemara] explains further on.

Rashi on Shabbat 103b:11:1.hebrew: אחת שמעון - כלומר, דריש מ"ם יתירה. "אחת" הוי משמע דאינו חייב עד שיכתוב כל התיבה שנתכוין לכתוב:
Rashi on Shabbat 103b:11:1.english: “One” — “Shimon” - That is to say, he expounds the superfluous [letter] mem [in “from one”]: “one” would have implied that one is not liable until he writes the entire word that he intended to write.

Rashi on Shabbat 103b:11:2.hebrew: מאחת שם משמעון - כתב מאחת למימר דאפילו לא כתב אלא מקצתה, ובלבד שתהא מקויימת במקום אחר, דומיא דאחת דרישיה דקרא:
Rashi on Shabbat 103b:11:2.english: "From one" — "Shem" from "Shimon" - [Scripture] wrote "from one" to say that even if he only wrote part of it, [he is liable,] provided that it is valid in another place, similar to "one" at the beginning of the verse.

Rashi on Shabbat 103b:11:3.hebrew: הנה הוי משמע אבות, כתב מהנה לרבויי תולדות:
Rashi on Shabbat 103b:11:3.english: “These” would imply primary categories [of labor]; [Scripture] wrote “from these” to include subcategories.

Rashi on Shabbat 103b:11:4.hebrew: אחת שהיא הנה - דאמרן לעיל, ה"ד? כגון שעשאן בזדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות. ואע"ג דכולן אינן אלא חילול שבת אחת, מיחייב לכל מלאכה ומלאכה, דגופי מלאכות מחלקין, הואיל ואיכא שגגה טובא:
Rashi on Shabbat 103b:11:4.english: One that is these - which we said above, what is the case? For example, where he performed them with awareness of Shabbat and unawareness of [the prohibited] labors. And even though all of them are only one desecration of Shabbat, he is liable for each and every labor, for distinct categories of labor separate [the liabilities], since there is much unawareness.

Rashi on Shabbat 103b:11:5.hebrew: הנה שהיא אחת שגגת שבת וזדון מלאכות - שאף על פי שהן גופי מלאכות הרבה, אינו חייב אלא אחת, דחדא שגגה היא:
Rashi on Shabbat 103b:11:5.english: These that are one — unawareness of Shabbat and intentional [violation of] labors - For even though they are many distinct categories of labor, he is liable for only one [sin-offering], since it is a single [lapse of] unawareness.

Rashi on Shabbat 103b:12:1.hebrew: מי דמי כו' - זה שנתכוין לכתוב שם משמעון, מ"ם פתוחה כתב; והיכי קרי ליה מתקיימת במקום אחר? והא לא הויא:
Rashi on Shabbat 103b:12:1.english: Is it similar, etc. - This [person] who intended to write "Shem" from "Shimon" wrote an open mem; so how does [he] call it enduring in another place, when it is not?

Rashi on Shabbat 103b:13:1.english: And you shall write them - [This refers to] tefillin and mezuzah.

Rashi on Shabbat 103b:13:2.english: Perfect - Complete, in accordance with its halakha.

Rashi on Shabbat 103b:13:3.english: Alefs [as] ayins - There are those who write thus because they are similar in their pronunciation.

Rashi on Shabbat 103b:13:4.english: Beitin [as] kafin - They are similar in their writing.

Rashi on Shabbat 103b:13:5.hebrew: גמין צדין - דומין בכתיבתן, אלא שזה למעלה וזה למטה:
Rashi on Shabbat 103b:13:5.english: Gimmels [as] tzadis - They are similar in their writing, except that this one is above and that one is below.

Rashi on Shabbat 103b:14:3.english: Mems [as] samekhs - [This refers to] a closed mem, which resembles a samekh.

Rashi on Shabbat 103b:14:6.english: Wrote it - [Referring] to a Torah scroll.

Rashi on Shabbat 103b:14:7.english: Like a song - With spaces, [like] a half-brick and a whole brick.

Rashi on Shabbat 103b:15:1.hebrew: מכאן רמז כו' - כלומר, מ"ם דונסכיהם דריש ליה בפתוחה, [שמע מינה] בפתוח ועשאו סתום דכשר; ומדפתוח ועשאו סתום כשר, הוא הדין נמי סתום ועשאו פתוח, כגון שם משמעון, וכשר להתקיים במקום שם:
Rashi on Shabbat 103b:15:1.english: From here [there is] an allusion, etc. - That is to say, he expounds the mem of veniskeihem as an open [mem]; [one may infer from this] regarding an open [mem] that one made closed, that it is valid. And since an open [mem] that one made closed is valid, the same law [applies] as well [to] a closed [mem] that one made open, such as [writing] Shem from Shimon, and it is valid to remain in place of Shem.

Rashi on Shabbat 103b:1:1.hebrew: ת"ל אחת - שתהא מלאכה שלימה במקום אחד:
Rashi on Shabbat 103b:1:1.english: The verse states “one” - [Meaning] that it be a complete labor in one place.

Rashi on Shabbat 103b:1:2.hebrew: שם משמעון - ולגבי בגד נמי שני חוטין, ובנפה שני בתין, שמקיימין כך — לפי שאין אדם אורג בגד ביום אחד ועושה נפה בבת אחת, ומתחיל ועושה כדי קיום שלא יהא נסתר מאליו:
Rashi on Shabbat 103b:1:2.english: Shem from Shimon - And regarding a garment as well, [one is liable for] two threads, and in a sieve, two meshes, for they endure thus — because a person does not weave a garment in one day or make a sieve all at once, and he begins and makes [an amount] sufficient to endure, so that it will not come undone on its own.

Rashi on Shabbat 103b:1:3.english: Even [if] he did not write [it] - from a large word.

Rashi on Shabbat 103b:1:4.hebrew: אלא ב' אותיות של שם אחד כגון שש תת - והן מתיבות גדולות, כגון: שש — מששבצר, מששך, ששמם; תת — מתתראו, תתנו. וכ"ש אם נתכוין לקטנה תחילה:
Rashi on Shabbat 103b:1:4.english: Only two letters of one name, e.g., shesh, tet - And they are [written as part] of larger words, e.g., shesh from Sheshbazzar, from Sheshach, [or] sheshamam; tet from titra'u, [or] titnu. And all the more so [is he liable] if he intended [to write] the small [word] from the outset.

Rashi on Shabbat 103b:3:1.hebrew: שכיוצא בה מתקיימת - ולקמיה פריך: היינו ת"ק:
Rashi on Shabbat 103b:3:1.english: That is of the type that endures - And later [the Gemara] asks: That is [the same as] the Tanna Kamma.

Rashi on Shabbat 103b:4:1.hebrew: ר' יוסי אומר - מפרש למילתיה לקמן:
Rashi on Shabbat 103b:4:1.english: Rabbi Yosei says - [The Gemara] explains his statement below.

Rashi on Shabbat 103b:6:1.english: Is identical to the first tanna - [Both hold one is liable for] shesh [and] tet.

Rashi on Shabbat 103b:6:2.hebrew: וכ"ת אלף אלף דאאזרך - שהם שתי אותיות מתיבה גדולה, אבל לא מצינו שהיא תיבה קטנה בכל המקרא:
Rashi on Shabbat 103b:6:2.english: And if you say alef alef of a'azerkha - For they are two letters from a larger word, but we do not find that it is a small word anywhere in Scripture.

Rashi on Shabbat 103b:6:3.hebrew: כיון דאיתא בגלטורי - קמיעות וכתבים של מכשפות ושל שמות, קורין בלשון לטי"ן של מינין קלוטרוס, ורגילין סופרין לכתוב בהן תיבות של שתי אותיות, ואינם תיבות במקום אחר:
Rashi on Shabbat 103b:6:3.english: Since it appears in gelatorei - Amulets and writings of sorceresses and of [mystical] names are called keloteros in the Latin language of the heretics, and scribes are accustomed to write in them words of two letters that are not words elsewhere.

Rashi on Shabbat 103b:7:1.hebrew: הקודח כל שהוא - קצת הנקב, ואע"פ שלא עבר עובי העץ לראות בעבר השני:
Rashi on Shabbat 103b:7:1.english: One who drills any amount - [Meaning] part of the hole, even though he did not pass through the thickness of the wood to see [through] on the other side.

Rashi on Shabbat 103b:7:3.hebrew: המגרר - כלונסות או קלפים, דהויא תולדה דממחק:
Rashi on Shabbat 103b:7:3.english: One who scrapes - Poles or parchments, for it is a subcategory of smoothing.

Rashi on Shabbat 103b:7:4.english: All of it - Whatever he intended to scrape or to tan from the outset, at one time.

Rashi on Shabbat 103b:8:1.english: The entire name - The entire word.

Tosafot on Shabbat 103b:13:1.hebrew: טיתין פיפין - מכאן נראה לר"ת שצריך לכוף ראש הטית לתוכה, דדמי כעין פ':
Tosafot on Shabbat 103b:13:1.english: Tets [as] pehs - From here it appears to Rabbeinu Tam that one must bend the top of the tet inward, as it resembles a peh.

Tosafot on Shabbat 103b:15:1.hebrew: בשביעי כמשפטם גרסינן - כדמוכח בפרק קמא דתענית (דף ב:), וכן הוא במסורת הגדולה; ודלא כרש"י דגרס בשמיני בס"פ לולב וערבה (סוכה דף מז:):
Tosafot on Shabbat 103b:15:1.english: "On the seventh [day], kemishpatam [according to their laws]," we read [in the text] - as is proven in the first chapter of Ta'anit (2b), and so it is in the Masorah Gedolah; unlike Rashi, who reads [the text as] "on the eighth [day]" at the end of the chapter [entitled] Lulav VeAravah (Sukkah 47b):

Tosafot on Shabbat 103b:6:1.hebrew: א"א דאאזרך איכא בינייהו - לאו דוקא, דהא ת"ק פטר אפי' שתי אותיות משם אחד עד שיכתוב שם משמעון, אלא משום ר"ש נקטיה, דאפי' בהא מיחייב:
Tosafot on Shabbat 103b:6:1.english: Alef alef of a’azerkha is [the difference] between them - [This is] not exact, for the first tanna exempts even two letters of a single name unless one writes "Shem" from "Shimon"; rather, [the Gemara] mentioned it because of Rabbi Shimon, for even in this [case] he holds [one] liable.

Tosafot on Shabbat 103b:6:2.hebrew: בגלטורי בעלמא חייב - פירוש: א"א שכותבין בקמיע, וכן פירש ר"ח. ויש מפרשים: א"א היינו אמן אמן (סלה) שכותבין בקמיעין. וליתא, דהיינו נוטריקון וחייב אפילו באחד, ורבנן דפטרי במתני' פטרי אפילו בב' וג':
Tosafot on Shabbat 103b:6:2.english: In standard amulets he is liable - Explanation: [This refers to the letters] alef alef that are written in an amulet, and so Rabbeinu Chananel explained. And some explain [that] alef alef means "Amen, Amen (Selah)" that is written in amulets. But this is not [correct], for that is notarikon [an acronym], and one is liable even for one [letter], whereas the Rabbis who exempt in the Mishnah exempt even for two or three.

Tosafot on Shabbat 103b:7:1.hebrew: המעבד כל שהוא - לאו דוקא כל שהוא, אלא כשיעור המפורש בהמוציא (לעיל דן עט:), ולא נקט כל שהוא אלא לאפוקי מדר"ש דאמר עד שיעבד כל העור:
Tosafot on Shabbat 103b:7:1.english: One who tans any amount - Not literally any amount, rather [it means] according to the measure explained in [chapter] Hamotzi (above, 79b); and [the Tanna] only stated "any amount" in order to exclude [the view] of Rabbi Shimon, who says [one is not liable] until he tans the entire hide.

Tosafot on Shabbat 103b:8:1.hebrew: תריץ הכי יכול עד שיכתוב כל הפסוק כו' - וא"ת: ומ"ש אריגה מהני, דהכא לא מחייב ר"ש עד שיתקן את כולו? וי"ל: דבאריג, שעושה דבר חדש שאינו בעולם, מחייב שפיר בשני בתי נירין; אבל עיבוד, שאינו אלא תיקון העור בעלמא, וכן גורר וצר צורה — בעי ר"ש עד שיתקן את כולו:
Tosafot on Shabbat 103b:8:1.english: Resolve [the contradiction and say] this: I might [have thought that one is liable only] if he writes the entire verse, etc. - And if you ask: How is weaving different from these [cases], where here Rabbi Shimon does not hold [one] liable until he completes the entire [thing]? One can answer: In weaving, where one makes something new that did not [previously] exist, [Rabbi Shimon] properly holds [him] liable for two heddles; however, [regarding] tanning, which is merely the improvement of the hide, and similarly scraping and drawing a figure — Rabbi Shimon requires that he complete the entire [thing].
